CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA
ORAL ORDER

(PER: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA) The petitioner in Criminal Petition No.200706/2025 being accused No.2 in Crime No.6/2024 of Lokayukta Police Station, Raichur, in Spl.Case No.132/2017 pending on the file of the learned II Additional and Sessions Judge & Special Court at Raichur, is seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409 420, 201 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and under Section 13(1)(c) of Prevention of Corruption Act (for short 'PC Act').
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR The petitioner in Criminal Revision Petition No.200037/2025 being accused No.4 in the above case is seeking to set aside the order dated 23.10.2024 passed in Spl.Case No.132/2017 referred to above rejecting his application for discharge.

2. Heard Sri Sanjay A.Patil learned counsel for the petitioner-accused No.2, Sri.Gururaj Gopal Rao,
learned counsel for the petitioner-accused No.4 and Sri. Subhash Mallapur, learned Special Public Prosecutor for the respondents.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the points that would arise for my consideration are:
(1) "Whether the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner in Crl.P.No.200706/2025 is liable to be quashed invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, [for short, 'the BNSS']?

3 NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR (2) Whether the order dated 23.10.2024 passed against the petitioner Crl.R.P.No.200037/2025 is liable to be set aside invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, [for short, 'the BNSS']?"

sentences.text:
4. My answer to the above points is in the 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 5.
It is the contention of the petitioners in both petitions that Crime No.6/2014 of Lokayukta Police Station, Raichur came to be registered against accused Nos.1 to 7.
Investigation was undertaken and final report came to be filed for the above said offences.
Learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences.
Now the matter is pending in Spl.C.No.132/2017 on the file of learned II Additional and Sessions Judge & Special Court at Raichur.

sentences.text: Both accused Nos.2 and 4 appears to have filed separate applications seeking their discharge.
The NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR said applications came to be dismissed by the Trial Court by passing similar orders.

Accused No.2 filed Criminal Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him, while accused No.4 filed revision petition challenging the order of dismissing the application for discharge.
6. The only ground urged by both the petitioners either to seek quashing of the criminal proceedings or to set aside the order passed by the Trial Court rejecting the application for discharge.

The circular issued by the State Government dated 28.03.2023, which reads as under;

On perusal of the proceedings of the Government, it is clear that the Government was appraised with the problems that are being faced by the Investigating Officer in investigating such offences which are highlighted as under:

sentences.text: (i) It is highlighted that, the job cards issued under the scheme were 10 to 15 years old since the persons who worked under the scheme have already migrated to other places.
Even the Investigating Officer was not in a position to verify such job cards.
(ii) The work carried out in the land of an agriculturist about 10-15 years earlier has lost its original condition and therefore the work undertaken about a decade ago could not be verified.

(iii) Dredging a lake, development of road, are the work under the scheme which are carried out long NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR back and no evidence could be made available to cross verify the execution of work.
(iv) From the year 2007-08 to 2011-12, full fledged MIS system was not in force and therefore the information about the same is not available.
(v) Construction of check dam and C.C. roads have lost their identity due to natural calamites and their construction long back is not verifiable.
(vi) Since the incident is more than 10-15 years back, the labourers are not in a position to give their statement recollecting the work undertaken by them.

(vii) Many of the Panchayat Secretaries working in various Gram Panchayats are either retired or promoted as Panchayat Development Officers and transferred to other places or in many cases they have died.
Hence, their assistance could not be taken.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR (viii) The original records found in the bank and post office have already been destroyed and same are not available for verification.

(ix) Karnataka Lokayukta Police are involved in investigation into the cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act and they are not in a position to complete the investigation in the present cases by verifying all such works undertaken during the period of 5 years.

(x) During the period of 5 years, under MGNREGA scheme about 9.86 Lakhs works were undertaken in 30 Districts of State and verification of all those works and documents will take sufficiently long period of time.
(xi) Taking into consideration all these difficulties faced by the Investigating Officer, the investigation that was entrusted to Lokayukta Police was withdrawn.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that in view of circular dated 28.03.2023, the case registered by Lokayukta Police pertaining to Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) scheme was withdrawn and therefore the petitioners are entitled to seek quashing of the criminal proceedings or to set aside the order of the Trial Court dismissing the application for discharge.

entities.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) scheme
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The same cannot be accepted as no such meaning could be made out from the circular dated 28.03.2023.
On the other hand, it makes clear that, only the investigation in such cases were withdrawn.
Since the wordings in the circular is very clear to state that the investigation only in those cases referred to therein have been withdrawn.
In the present case the investigation is completed and charge sheet is already filed.
Now the matter is pending before the Trial Court for trial.

Therefore, it cannot be brought within the purview of the circular dated 28.03.2023.
- 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR 9.

Once the Investigating Officer files the final report and the Trial Court takes cognizance of the offence as highlighted in the final report, the Investigating Officer becomes functus official and he cannot be permitted to withdraw such proceedings without recourse to the procedure as contemplated in the then Criminal Procedure Code or the present Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
10. The Investigating Officer in the present case has already filed final report with voluminous documents which makes out prima-faice case based on which the cognizance was taken.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that it is not a fit case to quash the criminal proceedings or to set aside the order.
The Trial Court after taking into consideration all the materials on record, passed the order dated 23.10.2024.
I do not find any reasons to quash the criminal proceedings or to set aside the order of the Trial Court rejecting the application for discharge.

In view of the above, I answer above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
- 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4512 HC-KAR ORDER
Both the Criminal Petition No.200706/2025 and Criminal Revision Petition No.200037/2025 are hereby dismissed.
